target: Route "treewidth": Bounded width: a seventh polynomial class, or the exact place where interface tables explode

findings.defect: The claim that the piece explosion is "impossible at interface dimension one, so the threshold is located exactly" is contradicted by the route's own tw:fold-width, and is repeated verbatim in the paste-ready LaTeX (tw.tex line 929: "Cref{tw:one-live} forbids it at interface dimension one"). tw:one-live's hypothesis is not one-dimensionality of the interface; it is (a) the whole game acyclic and (b) every theta-dependent vertex has AT MOST ONE theta-dependent successor. Under the parameter reading of "interface dimension", thm:fold is a direct counterexample. Under the "live successors" reading of tw:one-live-remark, "dimension" is a misnomer and no threshold is located, since pathwidth 2 and 3 are both open. The statement must be withdrawn and replaced by the honest one: tw:one-live rules out folding only under a chain-shaped live-value hypothesis; tw:fold-width exhibits folding at pathwidth 4; everything between is open.
findings.evidence: tw:fold-width itself: "partial A = {u,t0,t1} ... R_A is a function of the SINGLE free parameter theta = varphi_u" and "the coordinate of R_A at F_D has exactly 2^D affine pieces". One free parameter, 2^D pieces. I reproduced the family and the width numbers: my own independent subset-DP gives tw(P_1..P_4) = 2,3,3,4 (/tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-tw/pd2.py, pd2.out).

findings.result_name: next_steps item 4 ("USE tw:qp AS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT ON THE PIVOT")
findings.defect: Category error at exactly the point the root agent would act on it. tw:qp bounds the cost of SOLVING an instance; the paper's open pivot asks for a family whose ALL-SWITCHES RUN is superpolynomial. Bounded treewidth is no obstruction whatever to that, so "a genuinely hard instance must have treewidth omega(1)" is not a usable filter on candidate all-switches families, and the instruction that it "should be applied to G# and to any realisation of thm:blowup's second level" would discard exactly the constructions the pivot needs. The route's own tw:qp-remark says the correct thing ("they were never hard to solve; they are hard for particular mechanisms ... a width bound says nothing about that"); next_steps contradicts it.
findings.evidence: L_n has tw = pw = 3 (route's own measurement, and I confirm the ladder is acyclic, mu_max = mu_min = mu_avg = 0, hence linear-time by thm:kacyclic), while thm:ladder gives least-index 2^n - 1 switches and all-switches n. Solvability and rule-hardness are independent, so a width bound filters neither.

findings.defect: On stopping games this is dominated by thm:bounded-components, which the route never compares it with (it compares only with tw:modulator and calls it "as far as the author knows, not recorded"). Every SCC of H(G) of size >= 2 consists of Max vertices mutually reachable by positive-length paths, hence lying on directed cycles of G; so max SCC size <= max(1, f_max) and thm:bounded-components already gives poly(N) 2^{f_max}. For k = min the same follows from thm:bounded-components applied to the dual game (lem:duality). The genuine increment is only that tw:colour-feedback needs no stopping hypothesis, and that should be the stated content.
findings.evidence: def:maxreach (u -> v iff v reachable from u by a positive-length path) plus thm:component-bound's sum_j (2^{|C_j|} - 1); mutual reachability of u and v gives a closed walk through u, hence a cycle through u, so a nontrivial SCC is contained in {Max vertices on cycles}.

findings.defect: Substantially a restatement of the paragraph immediately preceding thm:fold in sec:fold, plus lem:monotone, presented as a new proposition with a fresh proof. sec:fold already asserts, for the one-parameter case: "is piecewise affine, monotone and 1-Lipschitz, and its pieces are exactly the regions on which the optimal pair is constant". The genuine additions are the multi-dimensional boundary, the 2^{|C cap A|} piece bound and equivariance in the FULL terminal payoff vector (the last being a real correction the route found and reports honestly).

findings.defect: The "300 games / 616773 cut-map queries / 0 mismatches" headline does not test the recursion. Instrumenting the route's own harness at its deepest setting (t_alg3 generator, exact treewidth 3, base = 3, fresh seed 777, 20 games) gives maximum recursion depth 2, with 15436 of 15618 internal solve calls terminating immediately by backward induction, 110 at the brute-force base, and only 72 separator recursions in total (52 of them below the root). The regime the proof's bit-size recursion delta_{j+1} <= 3 delta_j + 4n describes -- nested Tarski searches over grids whose denominators compound -- is essentially unexercised. The theorem is proved, so this is corroboration, not support; the numbers should be described as such.

verdict:
IS IT NEW? Mostly yes, and the route's own attribution is unusually good. "treewidth" and "modulator" appear nowhere in frontier.tex. tw:tarski is correctly attributed to Etessami-Papadimitriou-Rubinstein-Yannakakis (with the honest note that they already reduce SSGs to Tarski in dimension N); tw:modulator is correctly attributed to Auger-Coucheney-Strozecki as the fvs special case; tw:qp is explicitly flagged as a candidate rediscovery. Three overlaps the route did NOT flag: tw:colour-feedback is dominated by thm:bounded-components on stopping games (see findings), tw:response is mostly the prose paragraph above thm:fold in sec:fold, and tw:fold-width is thm:fold plus a width computation.

CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? No. No oracle here is target-equivalent: tw:modulator's residual solver is thm:kacyclic, a proved polynomial algorithm; tw:qp recurses on strictly smaller games with a brute-force base case. There is no claimed BARRIER anywhere in this route -- tw:one-live, tw:no-clock and tw:fold-width are statements about DP tables and cover NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6, def:bsi; they must not be filed under barriers. The polynomial class IS nonempty and outside the six: I rebuilt M_n independently and confirmed by brute-force max-min on the subgame reachable from h (it is all of it) for n = 3..6 -- stopping, val(h) = 1/2 + 2^{-(n+1)}, value-vector lcm denominator exactly 2^{n+1}, alphabet n+3, a = 3n, not max/min/avg-acyclic, H(M_n) a single SCC of size n+1, no feedback vertex set of size <= n (exhaustive, n = 3,4), and mu_max = 1 (the single-vertex max-modulators are exactly the 3n+1 ring vertices). M_n is a genuine family (build(n), growth law proved via lem:successor-closed onto thm:vi-lower's G_n, verified at 10 sizes), stopping, legitimate under def:ssg, and it is the paper's FIRST instance outside all six classes.

IS THE VERIFICATION HONEST? Yes, and unusually so -- the route reports a refuted first version of tw:response and a looping first version of tw:tarski, and labels tw:gap2-shape's random half as "no evidence at all". Everything I re-ran reproduced: modulator.py on M_n (10-11 queries, exact, T w = w, n <= 12); tw:cyclic (4 queries, val(u) = 1/2 + 3*2^{-(D+3)}, D = 2..12); tw(P_1..P_4) = 2,3,3,4 by my own independent subset DP; pw(P_D) <= 4 by explicit decomposition to D = 60; tarski_fp on 500 FRESH random monotone maps (0 failures, mean 11.5 queries); the tw:qp algorithm on a fresh seed, 80 games (0 mismatches). The one honest-verification defect is depth, not correctness: the separator recursion is only two levels deep in the validation set (see findings).

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. The route's GAP 1 asks for N^{f(k)} at treewidth k; the true missing statement is the amortisation lemma that would give it, and it should be stated as such: "the O(B^{k+1}) payoff vectors at which a separator node queries its children during one Tarski search can be answered in total time polynomially related to the time to answer one of them" -- because a piece-count bound, the other route to N^{f(k)}, is killed by tw:fold-width. But the sharper gap is one the route does not state at all: BOTH halves are off the target. The paper wants general SSG in P; treewidth is a parameter no reduction bounds, and the seventh class is empty at the frontier (min_k mu_k = 0 on every stalling instance of sec:gap that I could test). The route's only on-target deliverable is that it answers a question rem:kacyclic explicitly poses, and the honest one-sentence gap is: "no instance with mu_k > 0 is known that stalls any mechanism of sec:gap, so the modulator class, like the escape class, cannot reach the frontier."

WOULD INTEGRATING THIS MAKE THE PAPER BETTER? Better, but only about half of it, and only with edits.

INTEGRATE: tw:modulator + tw:modulator-def + tw:kacyclic-mu + tw:family (M_n) + tw:cut-sign + tw:round + tw:recover + tw:tarski (with its attribution remark). This is the real content: it answers the question rem:kacyclic leaves open, it supplies the paper's first family outside all six classes, and it strictly beats the feedback-vertex parameter (mu_max = 1 against fvs >= n+1, both verified). It must be integrated with the rem:escape-class-style caveat that no frontier instance has mu_k > 0.

INTEGRATE WITH REWRITING: tw:qp and tw:qp-remark. The proof is coherent (I checked the bit-size recursion delta_{j+1} <= 3 delta_j + 4n, the convexity step sum_i T(n_i) <= 2T(n/2), the denominator bound Q = Delta 2^a, and the self-certification), the result genuinely beats thm:subexp and thm:few-avg in its regime, and the literature remark is careful. But it introduces a whole new parameter into a 137-page document that has none, it is the single most likely rediscovery in the round, and it does not advance the target. Keep it as a short subsection with the flag intact; delete next_steps item 4 entirely.

DO NOT INTEGRATE: tw:one-live, tw:no-clock, tw:gap2-shape and tw:fold-remark as a group. They serve GAP 2 -- whether the table explodes at pathwidth 3 rather than 4 -- which has no consequence for anything in the document, they cost four environments and two searches, and one of them carries a false headline claim. Compress to a single remark under tw:fold-width. tw:colour-feedback should either be dropped or restated as "thm:bounded-components without the stopping hypothesis, via freezing". tw:response should be folded into sec:fold as the multi-dimensional form of the paragraph already there. tw:fold-width's width numbers are worth one sentence, not a theorem.
